speciesDescription: A large sea turtle with a reddish-brown carapace, a large head, and powerful jaws. It occurs in the Pacific and Indian Oceans, including Indonesia.
diet: Carnivorous; commonly eats hard-shelled marine invertebrates.
habitat: Open ocean, coastal waters, bays, lagoons, estuaries and feeding grounds such as reefs and rocky areas.
distribution: Pacific, Indian and other major ocean regions; occurs in Indonesian waters.

speciesDescription: A sea turtle named for its light brown to olive-colored appearance. Its range includes the Pacific and Indian Oceans.
diet: Omnivorous; feeds on a range of marine animals and plant material.
habitat: Tropical and subtropical marine waters, coastal areas and sandy nesting beaches.
distribution: Pacific and Indian Oceans, including Indonesia.

speciesDescription: A large marine turtle recognized by its greenish shell coloration and green body fat. It lives in tropical and subtropical seas.
diet: Primarily herbivorous as an adult, especially seagrasses and algae.
habitat: Tropical and subtropical marine waters, shallow coastal feeding grounds and nesting beaches.
distribution: Tropical and subtropical oceans worldwide, including Indonesian waters.

speciesDescription: The nominate hawksbill form, characterized by a pointed bird-like beak and overlapping scutes on the shell. It groups under the hawksbill sea turtle and describes the species as having a distinctive beak.
diet: Primarily sponges and other reef-associated invertebrates.
habitat: Coral reefs, rocky coastal habitats, lagoons and other tropical marine areas.
distribution: Tropical Atlantic and Indo-Pacific regions; the hawksbill occurs in Indonesian waters.

speciesDescription: An Indonesian hawksbill subspecies with the characteristic narrow, pointed beak and overlapping shell scutes of Eretmochelys imbricata. It is one of the two hawksbill subspecies in its Indonesian list.
diet: Primarily sponges and other reef-associated invertebrates.
habitat: Coral reefs, lagoons, shoals and shallow tropical marine habitats.
distribution: Indo-Pacific; associated with Indonesian waters.

speciesDescription: A marine turtle named for its relatively flat carapace. It's shell is flat and uses this feature as the basis for the common name.
diet: Omnivorous; feeds on marine invertebrates and other available food.
habitat: Marine coastal waters over the continental shelf.
distribution: Northern Australia and nearby Indo-Pacific waters, including Indonesian waters.

speciesDescription: The largest living sea turtle, with a distinctive leathery body and shell. It is the largest sea turtle.
diet: Primarily jellyfish and other soft-bodied marine invertebrates.
habitat: Open ocean and coastal marine waters; nests on sandy beaches.
distribution: Widely distributed in tropical and temperate oceans, including Indonesian waters.

speciesDescription: A river terrapin associated with brackish waters where rivers meet the sea. It is called Tuntong Sungai and the nominate subspecies occurs on Sumatra.
diet: Omnivorous; aquatic vegetation and animal matter.
habitat: Large rivers, estuaries and brackish tidal waters.
distribution: Southeast Asia; in Indonesia, the listed subspecies occurs on Sumatra.

speciesDescription: A striking river turtle with a reddish head and a carapace marked by three horizontal lines.
diet: Omnivorous; aquatic plants and animal prey.
habitat: Rivers, tidal channels, estuaries and other lowland aquatic habitats.
distribution: Borneo and the Malay Peninsula; occurs in Indonesian Borneo.

speciesDescription: A highly aquatic box turtle with a domed shell and a hinged plastron that allows the limbs and head to be withdrawn. It is one of the Indonesian subspecies of Cuora amboinensis.
diet: Omnivorous; aquatic plants, invertebrates and other food items.
habitat: Warm freshwater habitats such as ponds, marshes, rice fields and slow-moving waters.
distribution: Indonesia and other parts of Southeast Asia; associated with the Wallacean region.

speciesDescription: A Southeast Asian box-turtle form with a hinged plastron and strongly aquatic habits. It is one of the Indonesian subspecies of Cuora amboinensis.
diet: Omnivorous; aquatic plants, invertebrates and other food items.
habitat: Warm, wet freshwater habitats including marshes, ponds, rice paddies and slow waters.
distribution: Western Indonesia and mainland Southeast Asia.

speciesDescription: A box-turtle form with a hinged plastron that helps it close the shell. It is one of the three subspecies of Cuora amboinensis found in Indonesia.
diet: Omnivorous; aquatic plants, invertebrates and other food items.
habitat: Warm freshwater wetlands, ponds, marshes, rice paddies and slow-moving waters.
distribution: Southeast Asia, including parts of Indonesia.

speciesDescription: A leaf turtle named for its leaf-like form and coloration. It has a brown carapace and yellow plastron that help it blend into forest surroundings.
diet: Omnivorous; fruits, plants, invertebrates and carrion.
habitat: Forest streams, wetlands, ponds and other freshwater habitats.
distribution: Indonesia and mainland Southeast Asia, including Sumatra, Java and other islands.

speciesDescription: A leaf turtle distinguished by an oval, somewhat rounded carapace with lines and spots. It differs in appearance from Cyclemys oldhamii and Cyclemys dentata.
diet: Omnivorous.
habitat: Freshwater rivers and swamps.
distribution: Sumatra and parts of the Greater Sunda region and southern Malay Peninsula.

speciesDescription: A turtle with a strongly keeled, spiny-edged carapace. Its juvenile shell spines resemble rays or teeth and become less pronounced as the turtle grows.
diet: Omnivorous; vegetation, fruits and small animal prey.
habitat: Humid lowland and hill forests, especially near clear streams.
distribution: Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia and parts of the Philippines.

speciesDescription: A dark forest turtle with a distinctive pale or white beak and head markings. It is also known as the parrot-beaked or white-headed turtle.
diet: Omnivorous.
habitat: Humid tropical forest, streams and associated freshwater habitats.
distribution: Endemic to Sulawesi, Indonesia.

speciesDescription: A relatively flat-shelled Asian turtle distinguished by its noticeably flattened carapace.
diet: Omnivorous.
habitat: Forested freshwater habitats, streams, ponds and wetlands.
distribution: Southeast Asia, including Indonesia.

speciesDescription: A very large, dark freshwater turtle that can reach approximately one meter or more in carapace length. It is sometimes confused with other large Southeast Asian river turtles.
size: Up to 100 cm or more in carapace length
diet: Omnivorous.
habitat: Large rivers, lakes, swamps and other lowland freshwater systems.
distribution: Borneo, including Indonesia and Malaysia.

speciesDescription: A dark freshwater turtle with a mostly black body and contrasting pale or white markings on its head and plastron. It is also known as the white-cheeked turtle.
size: Up to about 20 cm carapace length
diet: Omnivorous.
habitat: Marshes, ponds, swamps, slow streams and other freshwater wetlands.
distribution: Mainland and island Southeast Asia, including Indonesia.

speciesDescription: A terrestrial tortoise with an oval shell and contrasting yellow and black coloration. It is a land tortoise native to Indonesia.
diet: Herbivorous; leaves, fruits, flowers and other plant material.
habitat: Humid tropical forests and forest-floor habitats.
distribution: Sulawesi and nearby Indonesian islands.

speciesDescription: The nominate subspecies of the Asian forest tortoise, known in Indonesia as Kura-kura Kaki Gajah. It is one of the two recognized subspecies of Manouria emys.
diet: Primarily herbivorous; grasses, leaves, fruits and other plant material.
habitat: Humid tropical forests and forest floors.
distribution: South and Southeast Asia, including Indonesia.

speciesDescription: A distinctive freshwater turtle with a pig-like snout, flipper-like limbs and a leathery shell. It is the only living species in the family Carettochelyidae.
diet: Omnivorous; aquatic plants, fruits and animal matter.
habitat: Rivers, lagoons, swamps and other freshwater environments in lowland tropical areas.
distribution: Northern Australia and southern New Guinea, including Indonesian Papua.

speciesDescription: A large softshell turtle with a dark body and yellowish spots. It is one of the Indonesian forms of Amyda cartilaginea.
size: Up to about 85 cm carapace length
diet: Omnivorous; aquatic animals, carrion and plant matter.
habitat: Rivers, ponds, swamps and other freshwater habitats.
distribution: South and Southeast Asia, including Indonesia.

speciesDescription: A softshell form of Amyda cartilaginea with the species' characteristic dark body and spotted appearance. It is one of the forms occurring in Indonesia.
size: Up to about 85 cm carapace length
diet: Omnivorous; aquatic animals, carrion and plant matter.
habitat: Rivers, ponds, swamps and other freshwater habitats.
distribution: Indonesia and surrounding Southeast Asian regions.

speciesDescription: A large narrow-headed softshell turtle with a distinctive elongated head and patterned carapace. Its shell markings often create a complex, batik-like appearance.
size: Up to about 140 cm carapace length
diet: Carnivorous; fish, aquatic invertebrates and other animal prey.
habitat: Large rivers and sandy or muddy freshwater bottoms.
distribution: Mainland Southeast Asia.

speciesDescription: A Javanese form of the narrow-headed softshell turtle with a large body, elongated head and a patterned carapace.
size: Up to about 140 cm carapace length
diet: Carnivorous; fish and other aquatic animals.
habitat: Large freshwater rivers and associated sandy or muddy habitats.
distribution: Java, Indonesia.

speciesDescription: A brown forest softshell turtle with dark markings across its body. It is adapted to freshwater habitats and is distinguished from larger softshell turtles by its relatively smaller size.
size: Up to about 35 cm carapace length
diet: Carnivorous/omnivorous; aquatic invertebrates and small vertebrates.
habitat: Forest streams, rivers, ponds and other freshwater habitats.
distribution: South and Southeast Asia, including Indonesia.

speciesDescription: A very large softshell turtle native to New Guinea. Like other members of the genus Pelochelys, it is an ambush-oriented predator that spends much of its time on river bottoms.
diet: Carnivorous; fish, crabs, mollusks and some vegetation.
habitat: Large rivers and muddy freshwater bottoms.
distribution: New Guinea, including Indonesian Papua.

speciesDescription: A very large freshwater softshell turtle adapted for ambush hunting. It often buries itself in sand or mud with only its head exposed while waiting for prey.
size: Up to about 200 cm carapace length
diet: Carnivorous; fish, crabs, mollusks and other aquatic prey.
habitat: Large rivers, estuaries and muddy freshwater bottoms.
distribution: South and Southeast Asia, including parts of Indonesia.

commonName: Northern New Guinea giant softshell turtle
speciesDescription: A large softshell turtle native to northern New Guinea. It belongs to the genus Pelochelys, whose members are highly aquatic turtles adapted to life in large freshwater systems.
diet: Carnivorous; fish and other aquatic prey.
habitat: Large rivers and muddy freshwater habitats.
distribution: Northern New Guinea, including Indonesian Papua.

speciesDescription: A long-necked side-necked turtle native to the New Guinea region. Like other Chelodina turtles, it folds its head sideways beneath the edge of its shell rather than pulling it directly backward.
diet: Carnivorous; fish, aquatic invertebrates and other small prey.
habitat: Freshwater rivers, swamps, ponds and wetlands.
distribution: New Guinea and northeastern Australia; occurs in Indonesian Papua.

speciesDescription: A long-necked side-necked turtle belonging to the genus Chelodina. Its elongated neck is adapted for capturing aquatic prey.
diet: Carnivorous; aquatic prey.
habitat: Freshwater rivers, swamps and wetlands.
distribution: New Guinea region, including Indonesia.

speciesDescription: A long-necked side-necked turtle from New Guinea with an elongated neck and head. It is adapted to freshwater habitats and captures fish and other small aquatic prey.
diet: Carnivorous; fish and aquatic invertebrates.
habitat: Freshwater rivers, lakes, swamps and wetlands.
distribution: New Guinea, including Indonesian Papua.

speciesDescription: The nominate form of the Rote Island snake-necked turtle, distinguished by its exceptionally long neck and restricted distribution on Rote Island.
diet: Carnivorous; fish, aquatic invertebrates and other small prey.
habitat: Freshwater lakes, ponds, swamps and slow-moving waters.
distribution: Rote Island, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia.

speciesDescription: A long-necked freshwater turtle representing a distinct form within the Chelodina mccordi complex and associated with the northern part of Rote Island.
diet: Carnivorous; fish and aquatic invertebrates.
habitat: Freshwater wetlands, ponds and slow-moving waters.
distribution: Northern Rote Island, Indonesia.

speciesDescription: A long-necked freshwater turtle associated with the Timor region and classified as a form within the Chelodina mccordi complex.
diet: Carnivorous; fish and aquatic invertebrates.
habitat: Freshwater ponds, wetlands and slow-moving waters.
distribution: Timor and nearby Indonesian islands.

speciesDescription: A long-necked side-necked turtle distinguished by distinctive markings on its head and an elongated neck adapted for capturing aquatic prey.
diet: Carnivorous; aquatic prey.
habitat: Freshwater rivers, swamps and wetlands.
distribution: New Guinea region, including Indonesian Papua.

speciesDescription: A long-necked side-necked turtle with an elongated neck and a complex taxonomic history. It is adapted to freshwater wetlands, rivers and swamps.
size: Up to about 40 cm carapace length
diet: Carnivorous; aquatic prey.
habitat: Freshwater wetlands, rivers and swamps.
distribution: Northern Australia and southern New Guinea.

speciesDescription: A large side-necked freshwater turtle from New Guinea, distinguished by its relatively pale plastron and adapted to rivers, streams and other freshwater environments.
diet: Omnivorous; aquatic plants and animal matter.
habitat: Freshwater rivers, streams, lagoons and wetlands.
distribution: New Guinea, including Indonesian Papua.

speciesDescription: A relatively small New Guinea side-necked turtle distinguished by its bright, pale plastron. It is adapted to freshwater rivers, streams and wetlands.
diet: Omnivorous; aquatic plants, invertebrates and other animal matter.
habitat: Freshwater rivers, streams and wetlands.
distribution: Western New Guinea, including Indonesian Papua.

speciesDescription: A New Guinea side-necked turtle associated with freshwater streams and rivers. It is a relatively recently described species within the genus Elseya.
diet: Omnivorous; aquatic plants, invertebrates and other animal matter.
habitat: Freshwater streams, rivers and wetlands.
distribution: Southern New Guinea, including Indonesian Papua.

speciesDescription: A New Guinea side-necked turtle distinguished by its pinkish-red plastron and coloration on parts of its limbs.
diet: Omnivorous; aquatic plants, invertebrates and other animal matter.
habitat: Freshwater rivers, streams and wetlands.
distribution: Northern New Guinea, including Indonesian Papua.

speciesDescription: A short-necked side-necked turtle distinguished by bright red or orange coloration on its plastron and limbs. It is one of the freshwater turtle forms occurring in the New Guinea region.
size: Up to about 30 cm carapace length
diet: Omnivorous; aquatic plants, invertebrates and small animals.
habitat: Freshwater rivers, streams, lagoons and swamps.
distribution: New Guinea and northern Australia; occurs in Indonesian Papua.
